name: calculus
title: Calculus
scope: This card applies limits, basic derivatives, and power integrals to the function already given.
method: Decide whether the question asks for a limit, a derivative, or an integral.
Rewrite the given expression as constants, sums, and powers before operating.
Differentiate with the power rule, the constant-multiple and sum rules, and the chain rule when there is an inside function.
For an indefinite integral of x^n with n not equal to -1, write x^(n+1)/(n+1) + C.
For a definite integral, evaluate F(b) - F(a) and treat it as net signed area.
If the function or the bounds are missing, stop and name what is missing.

formulas.name: Limit
formulas.use: L is the value f approaches as x approaches a, which need not equal f(a).

formulas.name: Power rule
formulas.use: Differentiates a constant power of x by bringing the exponent down and reducing it by one.

formulas.name: Constant multiple and sum rules
formulas.expr: d/dx [c f(x) + g(x)] = c f'(x) + g'(x)
formulas.use: A constant factor comes out of the derivative, and the derivative of a sum is the sum of the derivatives.

formulas.name: Chain rule
formulas.use: Differentiate the outer function, then multiply by the derivative of the inner function.

formulas.name: Power antiderivative
formulas.use: The antiderivative of a power uses this formula only when the exponent is not -1.

formulas.name: Definite integral
formulas.use: When F' = f, the fundamental theorem gives the net signed area from a to b.

checks: The power rule multiplies by the old exponent and then lowers that exponent by one.
The chain rule includes the derivative of the inside function.
The power antiderivative does not apply when n = -1.
A definite integral is net signed area, so the result can be negative.
limits: Product, quotient, and integration by parts are outside this card unless the expression reduces to the rules above.
A limit can exist when the function value at that point does not.
